body:
Three wall-clock-billed suites time out on the Windows runner, non-deterministically, and the cost lands on whichever PR is passing at the time.

OBSERVED three times on 2026-09-02..03, each on a PR whose diff could not plausibly reach the failing suites. The most recent is measured end to end (run 33707576978, PR #545):

- `test/browser/tutorial.test.ts:60` — hook timed out in 90000ms
- `test/cli/stock-refs.test.ts:281` — test timed out in 30000ms
- `test/federation/channel-record-trust.test.ts:628` — test timed out in 60000ms

No assertion failed in any of them. Linux was green on the same commit, `rails-guard` was green, and a re-run of ONLY the failed Windows job passed with no change to the tree — which is what makes this non-determinism rather than a defect.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT EXONERATES THE DIFF, and the one a future investigation should repeat first: the failing Windows job ran 10m02s (02:25:24 → 02:35:26) against main's last green Windows job at 9m36s (00:57:42 → 01:07:18). A 4.5% difference on a shared runner is not a diff that slowed the suite, and a run that bails early on three timeouts should be SHORTER than a green one, not longer.

WHY THIS CLASS. All three bills are wall-clock rather than work: a CDP browser hook, a CLI invocation, a federation record read. `HOST_SIZED_BILL_MS` is sized for one loaded suite, and the Windows runner is slower and more variable than the Linux one. The same shape is already recorded for concurrent local bars.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN AN ANNOYANCE. A red bar that a re-run clears trains whoever reads it to re-run rather than investigate, which deletes the value of red. The repo's own rule is that a flake is fixed the moment it is observed.

WHAT IS NOT THE FIX: widening these timeouts. That deletes the rail while appearing to repair it. The question to answer first is whether the bill should be wall-clock at all on a runner whose wall clock is this variable, or whether these three should bill work.

Acceptance criteria:
- (a) THE CAUSE IS NAMED BEFORE ANYTHING CHANGES: a run of the three suites on a Windows runner reports, per case, how much of its budget was spent waiting versus working. Verify: the CI log of a deliberate instrumented run, linked in the PR.
- (b) THE FIX IS NOT A WIDER TIMEOUT: whatever lands, the three cases still fail when the behaviour they assert is reverted, measured and reported as a revert probe. Verify: test/browser/tutorial.test.ts, test/cli/stock-refs.test.ts, test/federation/channel-record-trust.test.ts.
- (c) TEN CONSECUTIVE WINDOWS RUNS ON ONE UNCHANGED COMMIT ARE GREEN. Verify: ten linked CI runs.
- (d) IF IT CANNOT BE FIXED, IT IS AN HONEST SKIP: any case that cannot be made deterministic is `it.skip` carrying this ticket id in its title, never a widened assertion and never a retry loop. Verify: `npm run check`.
title: Three wall-clock-billed suites flake on the Windows runner
